checks.caption: Two transactions on a 1-seat event: the first books and pauses before its commit, the second runs up to its lock and waits for it. "Overbooked" means both got the seat. Per-transaction READ COMMITTED wasn't run on PostgreSQL, where it's already the default.
rows: Plain read, then the lock (the bug)
Capacity check in the lock's subquery, after a plain read

aria.arrivals: With a plain read before the lock, the share of overbooked events rose from 10.7% at 10 booking requests per second to 97.7% at 1,000. Locking first, READ COMMITTED, a counter on the locked row and PostgreSQL at its default isolation never overbooked an event.
aria.flash: With a plain read before the lock, a 10-seat event sold 11 seats with 2 bookers, 14 seats with 5 bookers, 19 seats with 10 bookers, 29 seats with 20 bookers, 59 seats with 50 bookers. Every fix sold exactly 10.
